finalArtMethod: Opt-in production combat/projectile trackers in the unchanged static or dynamic WebGL sample loop; measured counter collection runs after fenced timing. Per-cycle renderer.finalArt reports rules/catalog, event coverage, instance exposure and explicit unavailable measurements.

artMethod: Each of six layer lifetimes adds 12 warmup and 60 full real WebGL draws; fixed 280-unit snapshot, identical selection, deterministic timestamps, 1280x720 DPR1; gl.finish fences software GPU completion. FullDrawFenced includes CPU scene updates, WebGL submission and SwiftShader completion. CpuSubmission excludes finish. No simulation runs in this fixture; do not report these as hardware FPS.
method: Six cycles; ten real-WebGL hover-only cases per cycle for own/ally/enemy ground troops, deck crew and hulls plus sloped bridge crew, with per-instance position/color/height/stroke checks; real full-selection draws before/after CPU samples. 120 fixed-snapshot full-selection and 120 fresh-tick alternating-selection CPU draws per cycle; renderer.render disabled only during CPU timing, excluding GPU work. All disposed layer references retained intentionally to verify explicit release; GC requested through CDP. Teardown follows main.ts layer, request/decode, portrait and shared-model ordering. CPU samples are not device FPS.

combatStats.totalsMeaning: count/air/body/deck/speed are instance-frame exposure, drawCalls and overflow sum per-frame submissions/rejections. Capacity/bufferBytes/limit are peak gauges only, never allocation counts.

blood.counting: Deduplicated by real effect id within this layer lifetime. Replay cycles observe the same events; do not sum unique counts across cycles.

projectiles.unresolvedMeaning: Existing launch coordinates are retained when socket metadata is unavailable; unresolved is not proof of a missing projectile.

finalArt.scope: Production World3DLayer including combat/projectile tracker updates and GPU ink. Canvas terrain/ground blood pass is not timed. GPU instance counts do not establish visible fragment counts. History begins at the unchanged first warmup snapshot; older expired hit events cannot reconstruct ground residue.
